messages:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: Incident created (P1) - CI deploys failing. Root cause: GitHub Actions unable to fetch packages from GitHub Packages / npm mirror. Triggered at 2026-08-15T02:16:07Z. Pager sent to on-call.
Sara K: saw the alert, jumping in. CI is failing on the hotfix pipeline for release/v1.12.1 - build stage aborting on 'npm install' with 503 from github.packages. Error snippet: `GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@acme/lib - 503 Service Unavailable`.
Miguel R: confirmed, I can reproduce locally hitting same 503 for packages hosted on GH Packages. GitHub status shows partial outage for Actions and Packages: https://www.githubstatus.com/ - appears related.
Jen L: copying incident playbook: /incidents/runbooks/ci-thirdparty-outage.md. We need to assess customer impact and whether to rollback the release. Who is blocked by this hotfix?
Alice G: Support reports 3 mid-market customers on Dedicated saw delayed config updates (they depend on hotfix). No data loss, but feature gating is stuck. Estimated impact: medium-high for those customers.
Support Lead: noted, sending proactive note to affected customers with ETA placeholder. Avoid promising time until we have a workaround.
Miguel R: attempts to run alternative: switching registry to registry.npmjs.org for public packages helps but our private packages are only on GH Packages. Trying a mirror path.
Sara K: can we use artifact stash? Any recent CI artifacts with the prebuilt image for the hotfix?
Build Bot: artifact lookup: found last successful image for commit sha abcdef on staging (tag: staging-abcdef). No build for release/v1.12.1.
Miguel R: plan A: build the docker image locally from the hotfix branch and push to ECR, then update deployment manually. Plan B: try to pull packages from an internal npm mirror (artifacts.rwinf-internal). Which is faster?
Jen L: go Plan A for speed. Document steps and assign someone to run manual deploy. I'll coordinate comms. @Sara K can you run the build?
Sara K: taking it. Running local build now. Pasting commands:
```
# build and push to our ECR
docker build -t rwinf/hotfix:sha123 .
docker tag rwinf/hotfix:sha123 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/rwinf/hotfix:sha123
aws ecr get-login-password | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
docker push 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/rwinf/hotfix:sha123
kubectl set image deployment/frontend frontend=123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/rwinf/hotfix:sha123 -n prod
```
Build output: dependency fetch still fails during docker build for private package. Need to inject cached package tarball.
Miguel R: I have a cached tarball of the private package in S3 (s3://rwinf-cache/@acme-lib-1.2.3.tgz). Suggested Dockerfile tweak: add `COPY` of tarball and `npm ci --offline` using `npm install ./@acme-lib-1.2.3.tgz`.
Sara K: pulling tarball from S3 now and modifying Dockerfile, building...
Build Bot: build logs: `Step 12/28 : RUN npm ci --only=production` -> succeeds using local tarball. Image pushed.
Sara K: manual deploy done. Rolling update started. kubectl rollout status shows pods becoming ready.
Alice G: monitoring metrics and logs - no errors in frontend service after deploy. Customers should be unblocked once rollout completes.
Jen L: great. Can we get CI to be able to run future hotfixes while GH Packages is down? We need a short-term tweak to our pipeline.
Miguel R: adding fallback to pipeline: if GH Packages fetch fails, try internal S3 cache, then fail. I'll open PR to CI scripts to add retry + S3 fallback.
Sara K: filed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/422 - adds `--prefer-offline` logic and S3 artifact fallback.
Support Lead: sending updated note to impacted customers: informing them of manual workaround and ETA for full CI recovery.
Oncall Bot: Incident update (P1) — mitigation in place: manual build/deploy successful, customer impact reduced to 'degraded/notification delay'. Next action: vendor contact and follow-up for permanent CI fix. Assigned: Miguel R (vendor contact), Sara K (CI PR follow-through), Jen L (customer comms).
Jen L: contacting GitHub support directly, referenced incident 9876543, requested ETA for Packages restore. Also adding observability vendor (Sentry) to watch for regressions.
Miguel R: GitHub responded: investigating; no ETA. They've acknowledged higher error rate on Packages API. Link: https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/gh-packages-xyz
Alice G: do we need an RCA ticket? I propose postmortem focusing on dependency hardening (artifact mirroring, CI fallbacks). I'll create the incident ticket in JIRA: INF-3129 and assign postmortem owner.
Sara K: creating runbook update PR to include S3 fallback and manual deploy recipe.
Support Lead: marking customers for follow-up tomorrow. Good job team. :thumbsup:
Oncall Bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 2026-08-15T02:48:19Z — CI still degraded until vendor fixes. Will keep incident open for postmortem tasks.
